biography_short: The final Prophet of Islam, born in Makkah and migrated to Madinah. He led the early Muslim community through revelations and established the foundations of Islamic civilization. His life serves as the primary model (Sunnah) for Muslims worldwide.
biography_source: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Al-Rahiq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar) by Safiur Rahman al-Mubarakpuri.

biography_short: Abu Bakr, born Abdullah ibn Abi Quhafa, was a senior companion, the closest friend, and father-in-law of Muhammad, the Islamic prophet. He served as the first caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate, ruling from 632 until his death in 634. Abu Bakr was granted the honorific title al-Ṣiddīq by Muhammad, a designation that continues to be used by Sunni Muslims to this day.
biography_bn: আবু বকর, ছিলেন একজন আরব রাজনৈতিক ও ধর্মীয় নেতা যিনি রাশিদুন খিলাফত প্রতিষ্ঠা করেন এবং ৬৩২ সাল থেকে ৬৩৪ সাল তার মৃত্যুর আগ পর্যন্ত ইসলামের প্রথম খলিফা হিসেবে শাসন করেন। তিনি ছিলেন ইসলামের নবী মুহাম্মাদের একজন বিশিষ্ট সঙ্গী ও শ্বশুর। এছাড়াও আবু বকর সুন্নি ইসলামের অন্যতম একজন গুরুত্বপূর্ণ ব্যক্তিত্ব।
biography_de: Abū Bakr ibn Abī Quhāfa as-Siddīq war einer der ersten Anhänger des Propheten Mohammed und als Vater von Aischa bint Abi Bakr sein Schwiegervater. Nach Mohammeds Tod im Juni 632 herrschte er als dessen „Nachfolger“ bzw. „Stellvertreter“ (Kalif) bis zu seinem Tod über die Gemeinschaft der Muslime.

biography_short: Umar ibn al-Khattab, simply known as Umar, was the second Rashidun caliph, ruling from August 634 until his assassination in 644. He succeeded Abu Bakr and is regarded as a senior companion and father-in-law of the Islamic prophet Muhammad.
biography_bn: উমর ইবনুল খাত্তাব ছিলেন ইসলামের দ্বিতীয় খলিফা ও প্রধান সাহাবীদের অন্যতম। আবু বকরের মৃত্যুর পর তিনি দ্বিতীয় খলিফা হিসেবে দায়িত্বপ্রাপ্ত হন। উমর ইসলামী আইনের একজন অভিজ্ঞ আইনজ্ঞ ছিলেন। ন্যায়ের পক্ষাবলম্বন করার কারণে তাকে ফারুক উপাধি দেওয়া হয়। আমিরুল মুমিনীন উপাধিটি সর্বপ্রথম তার ক্ষেত্রে ব্যবহৃত হয়েছে। ইতিহাসে তাকে প্রথম উমর হিসেবেও উল্লেখ করা হয়। নামের মিল থাকার কারণে পরবর্তী কালের উমাইয়া খলীফাহ্ উমর বিন আবদুল আজিজকে দ্বিতীয় উমর হিসেবে সম্বোধন করা হয়। সাহাবীদের মর্যাদার ক্ষেত্রে সুন্নীদের কাছে আবূ বকরের পর উমরের অবস্থান। শিয়া সম্প্রদায় উমরের এই অবস্থান স্বীকার করে না। এছাড়াও তিনি ছিলেন ইসলামের নবী মুহাম্মাদ (সা:)এর শ্বশুর। উমর (রাযি)এর মেয়ে হাফসা বিনতে উমর ছিলেন মুহাম্মাদ(সা:)এর স্ত্রী।
biography_de: Umar [ˈʕumar] oder Omar ist ein männlicher Vorname arabischer Herkunft, der auch Teil eines Familiennamens sein kann. Die Schreibung Umar basiert auf der hocharabischen Phonetik, während Omar auf die dialektale Aussprache des Namens zurückgeht, die auch bei der Übernahme des Namens in die iranischen Sprachen prägend war. Das hocharabische kurze „u“ wird im dialektalen Arabisch und im Persischen meist zu einem kurzen „o“ abgeflacht. Seine Verbreitung verdankt er Umar ibn al-Chattab, dem zweiten der vier „rechtgeleiteten“ Kalifen des Islam.

biography_short: Uthman ibn Affan was the third caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate, ruling from 644 until his assassination in 656. Uthman, a second cousin, son-in-law, and senior companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad, played a major role in early Islamic history. During his reign as caliph, he was known for ordering the official compilation of the standardized version of the Quran, known as the Uthmanic codex, which is still used today.
biography_bn: উসমান ইবনে আফ্‌ফান ছিলেন ইসলামের তৃতীয় খলিফা এবং মুহাম্মদ সা. এর একজন প্রসিদ্ধ সাহাবি। তিনি ৬৪৪ থেকে ৬৫৬ সাল পর্যন্ত খিলাফতে অধিষ্ঠিত ছিলেন এবং খলিফা হিসেবে তিনি চারজন খুলাফায়ে রাশিদুনের একজন। উসমান ছিলেন আস-সাবিকুনাল আওয়ালুনের অন্তর্ভুক্ত। এছাড়াও তিনি আশারায়ে মুবাশ্‌শারার একজন এবং সেই ৬ জন সাহাবীর মধ্যে, অন্যতম যাদের উপর নবি মুহাম্মাদ অধিক সন্তুষ্ট ছিলেন। তাকে সাধারণত হযরত উসমান হিসেবে উল্লেখ করা হয়। তিনি কুরাইশ গোত্রের বিশিষ্ট বংশ বনু উমাইয়ায় জন্মগ্রহণ করেন। তিনি প্রথম দিকের ইসলামি ইতিহাসে অন্যতম প্রধান ভূমিকা পালনকারী।তিনি কুরআন সংকলনের আদেশ দেওয়ার জন্য পরিচিত ছিলেন।
biography_de: Uthman [ʕuθˈmaːn] ist ein Vorname arabischen Ursprungs. Seine Verbreitung verdankt er ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, dem dritten sunnitischen Kalifen. Der Name tritt auch als Familienname auf.

biography_short: The fourth Caliph and cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet. Renowned for his courage, eloquence, and deep knowledge of Islam. He is central to both Sunni and Shia traditions as a leader and spiritual authority.
biography_source: Nahj al-Balagha, Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Tarikh al-Tabari.

biography_short: One of the Ashara Mubashshara and a hero of the Battle of Uhud, where he protected the Prophet with his own body. Known as 'Talha al-Khayr' (Talha the Generous) for his immense charity.
biography_source: Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: One of the Ashara Mubashshara and the 'Disciple' (Hawari) of the Prophet. A brave warrior who participated in all major battles and was known for his loyalty and strength.
biography_source: Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Al-Isti'ab by Ibn Abd al-Barr.

biography_short: One of the Ashara Mubashshara (Ten Promised Paradise) and a very successful merchant who used his wealth for the cause of Islam. He was known for his extreme generosity and was one of the six members of the Shura council appointed by Umar.
biography_source: Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Al-Isti'ab by Ibn Abd al-Barr.

biography_short: One of the Ashara Mubashshara and a great military leader who led the Muslim army to victory at the Battle of Qadisiyyah against the Persians. He was the first to shoot an arrow in the cause of Islam.
biography_source: Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Tarikh al-Tabari.

biography_short: One of the Ashara Mubashshara and an early convert whose father, Zayd ibn Amr, was a seeker of monotheism before Islam. He was known for his piety and for avoiding political strife.
biography_source: Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: One of the Ashara Mubashshara and the 'Trustworthy' (Amin) of this Ummah. He was a key military commander in the conquest of Syria and known for his humility and asceticism.
biography_source: Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Tarikh al-Tabari.

biography_short: The first wife of the Prophet and the first person to accept Islam. She was a successful businesswoman known for her wisdom and virtue. She supported the Prophet during the most difficult early years in Makkah and is considered one of the 'Mothers of the Believers'.
biography_source: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: The wife of the Prophet and daughter of Abu Bakr. She was a prolific narrator of Hadith and a major scholar in early Islam, known for her intelligence and influence in jurisprudence and political matters.
biography_source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: The daughter of the Prophet and wife of Ali ibn Abi Talib. She is highly revered by all Muslims as a model of piety and patience, often called 'Az-Zahra'. Her descendants through Hasan and Husayn are the Ahl al-Bayt.
biography_source: Al-Isti'ab by Ibn Abd al-Barr, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: The eldest grandson of the Prophet and the fifth of the Rightly Guided Caliphs. He is highly revered for his wisdom and for abdicating the caliphate to Muawiya I in order to unite the Muslim Ummah and prevent further bloodshed.
biography_source: Al-Bidayah wan-Nihayah by Ibn Kathir, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: The younger grandson of the Prophet and a major figure in Islamic history. He is renowned for his refusal to pledge allegiance to Yazid I, which led to his martyrdom at the Battle of Karbala. His sacrifice is a symbol of resistance against injustice.
biography_source: Tarikh al-Tabari, Al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh by Ibn al-Athir, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: The uncle of the Prophet and 'Lion of Allah'. A legendary warrior who accepted Islam and became one of its strongest defenders. He was martyred at the Battle of Uhud.
biography_source: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar.

biography_short: The uncle of the Prophet and the ancestor of the Abbasid Caliphs. He accepted Islam and was highly respected by the Prophet and the early Caliphs for his wisdom and leadership among the Quraish.
biography_source: Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: An early convert of Abyssinian origin who was liberated from slavery by Abu Bakr. He became the first Mu'adhin (caller to prayer) of Islam and was known for his beautiful voice and steadfastness under torture. He participated in Badr, Uhud, and other major battles.
biography_source: Hilyat al-Awliya by Abu Nu'aym al-Isfahani, Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar.

biography_short: A brilliant military commander known as 'Saifullah' (The Sword of Allah). He remained undefeated in over a hundred battles, playing a decisive role in the expansion of the Islamic state in Iraq and Syria.
biography_source: The Sword of Allah: Khalid bin Al-Waleed by A.I. Akram, Al-Bidayah wan-Nihayah by Ibn Kathir.

biography_short: Daughter of the Prophet.
Daughter of the Prophet.
Daughter of the Prophet.

The cousin of the Prophet and the leader of the Muslims who migrated to Abyssinia. He was known for his eloquence in defending the Muslims before the Negus. He was martyred at the Battle of Mu'tah and was given the title 'At-Tayyar' (The Flyer in Paradise).
biography_source: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar.

biography_short: A beloved companion who was adopted by the Prophet before Islam. He is the only Sahabi mentioned by name in the Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab). He was martyred at the Battle of Mu'tah while leading the Muslim army.
biography_source: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar.

biography_short: The beloved of the Messenger of Allah.
Son of Umar and a great scholar of hadith.

The cousin of the Prophet and the preeminent scholar of the Quran, known as 'Habr al-Ummah' (The Scholar of the Ummah). He is one of the most prolific narrators of Hadith and a major authority in tafsir and jurisprudence.
biography_source: Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi, Tafsir Ibn Abbas.

biography_short: One of the earliest converts and a preeminent scholar of the Quran. The Prophet said, 'Whoever wants to recite the Quran as it was revealed, let him recite it according to the recitation of Ibn Umm Abd (Abdullah ibn Mas'ud).'
biography_source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar.

biography_short: A companion who spent several years in the company of the Prophet and became the most prolific narrator of Hadith. He was known for his incredible memory and devotion to preserving the words and actions of the Prophet.
biography_source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: A companion who served the Prophet for ten years in Madinah. He is one of the most prolific narrators of Hadith and lived a long life, during which he taught the Sunnah to many students.
biography_source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: A prominent companion from the Ansar who participated in many battles and was a major narrator of Hadith. He was known for his devotion to the Prophet and for his scholarship in Madinah.
biography_source: Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: One of the young Sahabah and hadith narrators.

A young and brilliant companion whom the Prophet described as the most knowledgeable of this Ummah in matters of Halal (permissible) and Haram (forbidden). He was sent to Yemen as a teacher and judge.
biography_source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: The master of reciters.
The primary scribe of the Quran.

An early convert and one of the most prominent ascetics among the Sahabah. He was known for his extreme truthfulness and his outspokenness in the face of what he perceived as deviations from the Prophet's path.
biography_source: Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Hilyat al-Awliya by Abu Nu'aym al-Isfahani.

biography_short: A Persian seeker of truth who traveled through several lands and converted to multiple religions before finding the Prophet in Madinah. He suggested the digging of the trench in the Battle of the Trench.
biography_source: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: One of the earliest converts to Islam who, along with his parents, endured severe torture for his faith. The Prophet called him 'the good one, the son of the good one.' He was martyred at the Battle of Siffin.
biography_source: Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: A brave companion who was one of the first seven to declare their Islam openly. He is famous for his courageous speech at the Battle of Badr, where he pledged the Muslims' unwavering support to the Prophet.
biography_source: Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: The keeper of the Prophet's secrets.
A brilliant strategist and diplomat who led the Muslim conquest of Egypt. He served as the governor of Egypt for several years and was known for his administrative skills and political acumen.
biography_source: Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Tarikh al-Tabari, Al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh by Ibn al-Athir.

biography_short: The first Caliph of the Umayyad Dynasty and a companion of the Prophet. He served as the governor of Syria for 20 years before becoming Caliph, during which he established the first Muslim navy and expanded the state's administrative capabilities.
biography_source: Al-Bidayah wan-Nihayah by Ibn Kathir, Tarikh al-Tabari, Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan by Ali Muhammad al-Sallabi.

biography_short: The first ambassador of Islam, sent by the Prophet to Madinah before the Hijrah to teach the people the Quran. He was a wealthy young man who gave up everything for Islam and was martyred at Uhud.
biography_source: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar.

biography_short: A prominent member of the Ansar who hosted the Prophet in his house when he first arrived in Madinah. He participated in many battles and died while participating in the siege of Constantinople.
biography_source: Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala by al-Dhahabi.

biography_short: The leader of the Aws tribe in Madinah. His acceptance of Islam led to the conversion of his entire tribe. He died from wounds sustained during the Battle of the Trench, and it is said the Throne of Allah shook at his death.
biography_source: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar.

One of the Mothers of the Believers and a woman of great wisdom and learning. She provided crucial advice to the Prophet at the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and was one of the last of his wives to pass away.

The first major military confrontation between the Muslims and the Quraish. Despite being outnumbered, the Muslims achieved a decisive victory, which significantly boosted the morale and status of the early Muslim community.
biography_source: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Quran (Surah Al-Anfal), Al-Maghazi by al-Waqidi.

biography_short: The second major battle between the Muslims and the Quraish. It was a tactical defeat for the Muslims after archers left their positions, leading to the martyrdom of many Sahabah, including Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib.
biography_source: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Quran (Surah Ali 'Imran), Al-Maghazi by al-Waqidi.

biography_short: A 27-day siege of Madinah by an alliance of Arab and Jewish tribes. The Muslims successfully defended the city by digging a trench around it, a strategy suggested by Salman al-Farisi.
biography_source: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab), Al-Maghazi by al-Waqidi.

biography_short: A battle fought against the Jewish tribes of Khaibar who had been inciting others against the Muslims. It resulted in a decisive Muslim victory and the capture of their fortresses.
biography_source: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Sahih al-Bukhari, Al-Maghazi by al-Waqidi.

biography_short: The first major encounter between the Muslims and the Byzantine Empire's forces. It resulted in the martyrdom of the three commanders appointed by the Prophet: Zayd ibn Harithah, Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, and Abdullah ibn Rawahah.
biography_source: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Al-Maghazi by al-Waqidi.

biography_short: A battle fought shortly after the Conquest of Makkah against the tribes of Hawazin and Thaqif. Despite an initial ambush, the Muslims rallied and achieved victory.

A major battle between the Muslim forces and the Byzantine Empire that resulted in a decisive Muslim victory, ending Byzantine rule in Syria. It is considered one of the most significant battles in military history.
biography_source: Tarikh al-Tabari, Al-Bidayah wan-Nihayah by Ibn Kathir.

biography_short: A decisive battle between the Muslim army led by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and the Sassanid Persian Empire. The Muslim victory led to the fall of the Persian capital, Ctesiphon, and the eventual conquest of Persia.
biography_source: Tarikh al-Tabari, Al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh by Ibn al-Athir.

biography_short: A powerful and efficient administrator who served as the governor of Basra and later Kufa under Muawiya I. He was known for his firm rule and for restoring order to the troubled provinces of Iraq.

Uthman ibn Amir ibn Amr, commonly known by the kunya Abu Quhafa, was the father of the first Rashidun caliph Abu Bakr.
Salma Umm al-Khayr bint Sakhar was a follower and companion (sahabi) of Islamic prophet Muhammad and the mother of Abu Bakr, the first Rashidun Caliph.

Aisha bint Abi Bakr was the third and youngest wife of Islamic prophet Muhammad. After Muhammad's death, she was politically active during the Rashidun Caliphate and stands out as a prominent female figure of the period.

Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr was a follower and Sahabiyya of prophet Muhammad and the elder half-sister of his wife Aisha. Her nickname Dhat an-Nitaqayn was given to her by Muhammad during the migration to Medina. She is regarded as one of the most prominent Islamic figures, as she helped Muhammad during the Hijrah from Mecca to Medina.

Zaynab bint ʿĀmir ibn ʿUwaymir ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAttāb al-Farāsīyya al-Kinānīyya, known by her kunya "Umm Rūmān" was among the followers or companions of Muhammad. As the wife of Abu Bakr and mother of Aisha, she was the mother-in-law of the Prophet of Islam.

name_ar: عبد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب
name_en: Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab
biography_short: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, commonly known as Ibn Umar, was a companion and brother-in-law of the Islamic prophet Muhammad and the most known son of the second Caliph Umar. The most prolific hadith narrator after Abu Huraira, Ibn Umar remained neutral during the events of the first Fitna (656–661).
Asim ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab was the son of Jamila bint Thabit and Umar ibn al-Khattab, the second Rashidun caliph. Asim was also a famous hadith scholar.

name_ar: عبيد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب
name_en: Ubayd Allah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab

biography_short: Zayd ibn ʿUmar, was a son of the second caliph Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and his wife Umm Kulthum bint Ali, a granddaughter of the Islamic prophet Muhammad.

Umm Kulthūm bint ʿAlī, also known as Zaynab al-Ṣughrā, was the youngest daughter of Fatima and Ali ibn Abi Talib. The former was the daughter of the Islamic prophet Muhammad and the latter was his cousin. Ali is also recognized as the fourth Rashidun caliph and the first Shia imam. A young Umm Kulthum lost her grandfather and mother in 632 CE. While she was still a child, the second Rashidun caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab asked for her hand in marriage, which was resisted by Umm Kulthum and her father Ali, possibly due to Umar's reputation for harsh treatment of women. By one Sunni account, Ali finally agreed to the marriage when Umar enlisted the support of prominent Muslims for his proposal.
Jamīla bint Thābit, originally named ʿĀṣiya, was a wife of Umar. She was among the disciples of Islamic prophet Muhammad.
Umm Kulthūm bint Jarwal, also known as Mulayka, was a wife of Umar and a follower or Sahabiyyah of the Islamic prophet Muhammad.
Zaynab bint Maẓʿūn was the first wife of Umar, the second Rashidun caliph.
Abu Uthman Amr ibn Uthman ibn Affan al-Umawi was a son of Caliph Uthman and played political and military roles during the caliphates of Mu'awiya I, Yazid I and Marwan I.

name_ar: عبد الله بن عثمان بن عفان
biography_short: Abdullah ibn Uthman, was the son of the third caliph Uthman and Ruqayya bint Muhammad. Born in Abyssinia, Abd Allah is believed by Sunni Muslims to be the first grandson of the Islamic prophet Muhammad.

Sa'id ibn Uthman ibn Affan al-Umawi was an Umayyad general and military governor of Khurasan in 676–677 during the reign of Caliph Mu'awiya I. He was a son of Caliph Uthman and a one-time seeker of the caliphate in 675/76.

Maryam bint al-Shaikh Uthman bin Fudi, also known by her title Uwardeji, was a scholar, teacher and influential figure in the Sokoto Caliphate. The youngest daughter of the Caliphate's founder, Usman dan Fodio, she was known for her learning and for her role in political and religious life in both Sokoto and Kano. She studied under her father and her sister Nana Asma'u, later becoming active in Asma'u's Yan Taru women's education movement, which she later led. Through her marriages, including to Emir of Kano Ibrahim Dabo, Maryam became connected to leading families of the Caliphate and played a mediating role in Kano–Sokoto relations. She was also regarded as an authority on Islamic eschatology, particularly debates surrounding the Mahdi in the late 19th century.
